report:
# Does Honey Help Against Acute Cough in Children? Yes—With Caveats

**Short answer: Yes**, evidence supports honey as a helpful, low-risk remedy for acute cough in children over age 1, though the quality of evidence is limited.

## The Evidence

A 2018 Cochrane systematic review (three RCTs, 568 children aged 1–18) found that honey **probably relieves cough symptoms to a greater extent than no treatment, diphenhydramine, and placebo**, and reduces cough duration better than placebo and salbutamol. However, honey **may make little or no difference compared to dextromethorphan**, a common OTC cough suppressant ([Cochrane, 2018](https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD007094_honey-acute-cough-children)).

A more recent 2023 systematic review, which added four new studies to the Cochrane analysis, confirmed and strengthened this conclusion: **"low quality evidence that honey may be more effective than cough medication or placebo/no treatment in relieving symptoms and improving sleep in children with acute cough"** ([PMC, 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10570220/)).

An earlier randomized trial comparing buckwheat honey, honey-flavored dextromethorphan, and no treatment similarly found honey benefited nocturnal cough and sleep quality ([JAMA Pediatrics](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapediatrics/fullarticle/571638)).

## Important Caveat: Age Restriction

Honey should **never be given to infants under 12 months old** due to risk of infant botulism from *Clostridium botulinum* spores, which can cause severe paralysis. This is confirmed by CDC, AAP, FDA, and poison control guidance ([Cleveland Clinic](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/infant-botulism); [Poison Control](https://www.poison.org/articles/dont-feed-honey-to-infants)).

## Conclusion

The evidence—though rated "low quality" due to small trial sizes—consistently supports honey as beneficial for cough symptoms in children over 1 year, comparable to or better than common OTC options, with minimal side effects. It should not be used in infants under 12 months.
